idiom_name: template text with markers resolved by a rendering engine against a prepared model
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the page as a text document containing markers, prepare a model before rendering, and let one engine pass over the template once, writing literal spans and substituting marker values (escaped for the context they land in) into the output stream. Decide once per template where static text ends and dynamic values begin, and put escaping in the engine rather than at the call sites. Layouts and partials give the repeated chrome one home: the template of a page composes fragments instead of repeating them. Where the engine can compile templates ahead of time, do it at startup so marker errors fail fast instead of on the first request.
code_sketch:
template:

{{ title }}

    {{#rows}}
  • {{ name }}
    • {{/rows}}
model: { title: "Orders", rows: [ { name: "A-100" }, ... ] } render: engine.render(template_path, model) -> output text # engine escapes every substituted value unless the marker is explicitly raw
pitfalls: Letting the template reach into the domain layer (queries, service calls, lazy relations) turns presentation into a second application.
One raw/unescaped marker is enough to void the engine's escaping guarantees; raw marks are security decisions, not formatting.
Skipping template compilation/caching re-parses the document on every request and moves marker errors to the request path.

Wrong move: building a template by concatenating user input into the template text (admin-editable page bodies, custom email copy) -> the engine evaluates the injected markers as template code and a request becomes remote code execution (server-side template injection) -> templates are authored by trusted people and reviewed like code; user data crosses only as model values through markers, and sandbox modes are mitigation, never a guarantee.

Wrong move: trusting the engine to report unknown or renamed markers -> interpreted engines resolve a missing key to an empty string by default (Go's html/template renders a nil value as empty), so a renamed field ships as a silently blank region -> enable strict/missing-key modes or use a compile-checked engine (Twirl, Razor, Askama) plus one golden render test per template.

Wrong move: rendering HTML with a text-oriented engine (Go's text/template, autoescape-off configurations) because the escaping 'looks simple' -> escaping is re-decided at every insertion point and the first missed attribute or script context is an XSS -> use the context-aware engine (Go's html/template) or turn autoescaping on instead of per-call-site discipline.
